seoTitle: Spectrogram Viewer: Draw an Audio File as an Image
metaDescription: Render a spectrogram of any audio file: time across, frequency up, colour for loudness. Linear or log axis, adjustable window. Free and private.
intro: Computes a short-time Fourier transform of an audio file and draws it as a picture with labelled time and frequency axes, which you can save as PNG.
why:
A spectrogram shows what a waveform hides: which frequencies are present and when. It reveals hum lines, hiss, clipping, a low-pass cutoff left by MP3 compression, bird calls, and the harmonics of an instrument.

Choose the window size to trade pitch detail against timing detail: 4096 samples separates close notes, 512 shows fast transients. A logarithmic frequency axis matches how we hear pitch; a linear axis shows high-frequency content better. Brighter colours are louder, over the dynamic range you set.
howTo: Pick the window size and the frequency axis.
Adjust the dynamic range (80 dB is a good start).
Press Run and save the image.

faq.q: What window size should I use?
faq.a: 2048 for general use, 4096 for pitch detail, 512 for drums and speech timing.

faq.q: Why does the top look empty?
faq.a: Many files have no content above 16 kHz because of MP3 compression or a low sample rate. That cutoff is useful to see.
No, it draws the whole file. The live spectrum analyzer shows the microphone in real time.

faq.q: How long a file can it draw?
faq.a: Several minutes. The image is capped at about 1400 columns, so long files lose some time detail.
